messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Sev2 - serving-pool-3 high error rate detected (RDMA link flaps) - paging oncall @Maya R
Maya R: picking up. seeing alerts: 5 nodes in serving-pool-3 flapping, several container restarts, multiple CUDA OOMs reported.
Maya R: initial customer impact: increased 5xxs and token latency spikes for a subset of dedicated customers in eu-west-1.
Ryan C: joining. can you paste the node list? I’ll start checking kernel logs and ib stats.
Maya R: nodes: gpu-3a, gpu-3b, gpu-7c, gpu-9f, gpu-12d. kube events show CrashLoopBackOff on model-serving pods, reason: container killed with SIGABRT then OOMs.
Priya S: I’m looking at routing. Traffic has been auto-failing to pool-fallback but fallback capacity is saturated. Canary pool is healthy.
Lucas H: Support reports customer A saw ~40% error rate for their generation routes since 09:12 UTC. They opened a ticket; they’re on a high-impact workspace.
Olivia L: escalation: keep Sev2 for now. If errors keep rising >30m, upgrade to Sev1.
Maya R: run this first check on node gpu-3a: 
```
sudo dmesg | tail -n 80 | grep -i -E "rdma|mlx|gdr|cuda|oom"
```
Maya R: on gpu-3a dmesg shows repeated mlx5 NIC resets and "IB CM: req timed out" followed by GDR errors: 
```
mlx5_core 0000:af:00.0: IB CM: port 1 failed, event REQ_TIMEDOUT
[email protected]: gdr_ioctl: device gone or internal error
"nvml: Xid 79" GPU crash (recovered)
```
Ryan C: that matches RDMA-level flaps. Running ibv_devinfo and perf query on the node.
Ryan C: ib link shows intermittent port state changes: 
```
# iblink -v
Port 1: ACTIVE -> DOWN (100 times in 6m)
```
Priya S: routing note: requests for model-xl are being redirected to model-lower for affected customers, but model-lower is CPU bound under the extra load.
Lucas H: Customer-facing update drafted: "We’re investigating an infrastructure issue causing higher error rates and latency for some inference requests in eu-west-1. Our SREs are actively mitigating. No data loss. We'll update in 30 minutes." Approve? :eyes:
Olivia L: send it, add note about failover behavior and we’re throttling some non-critical tenants to preserve BL.
Maya R: mitigation attempt 1: cordon + drain gpu-3a and move pods to other racks to break the RDMA path. Executed: `kubectl drain gpu-3a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.
deploy-bot: evicting pods from gpu-3a: 24 pods scheduled for reschedule.
Maya R: after drain, immediate network counters on switch show high retransmits on that port, but neighbor port also has errors. Suspect switch-level flapping.
Ryan C: collecting kernel traces and mlx logs, also pulling /var/log/syslog and dmesg from all 5 nodes.
Priya S: policy update: temporarily route traffic to Dedicated fallback region (eu-central-1) for affected customers where allowed. Initiating rolling route change for high-tier customers only.
Lucas H: applied customer-facing update v1.1 with time and mitigation steps.
Maya R: mitigation attempt 2: enable degraded-mode on runtime to reduce memory pressure: set env VAR REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DEGRADED=true for the pool, which forces smaller KV cache and disables some batching. Command: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/redwood-runtime REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DEGRADED=true -n serving-pool-3
```
Ryan C: curious — degraded mode might reduce OOM frequency but can increase token cost. We'll monitor.
Maya R: immediate effect: OOM events dropped from 7/min to 1/min on remaining nodes. Latency still elevated.
Olivia L: good. next: coordinate with infra to check switch fabric. @Priya S can you ping infra-network?
Priya S: pinged infra-network channel and opened infra ticket 2023-IR-889. Network confirmed they see CRC errors on the ToR that maps to rack 3. They plan to shift fabric paths and apply firmware patch if needed. ETA 25m.
Ryan C: until network patch, propose to move some pods to racks with healthy IB fabric (racks 7/8). I’ll run a controlled evac: `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force` is risky; prefer drain + reschedule with affinity override.
Maya R: proceeding with affinity override for non-critical replicas to speed migration.
Olivia L: coordinate with deploy-bot to limit concurrent evacuations to avoid load spikes. Set concurrency to 4 nodes at a time.
deploy-bot: initiating controlled eviction plan: concurrency=4, targetNodes=[gpu-7c,gpu-9f,gpu-12d,gpu-3b]
Ryan C: thanks. also running `ibv_devinfo -v` on candidate target nodes to confirm healthy MTU and link speed.
Priya S: routing change in progress, high-tier customers now pointed to eu-central-1 fallback; low-tier still on pool-3 (best-effort).
Lucas H: support update: Customer A's ticket updated with partial mitigation and expected timeframe.
Maya R: monitoring: errors trending down but still seeing sporadic CUDA Xid 79 on gpu-12d.
Ryan C: collected nvml logs, XID 79 indicates engine fault possibly triggered by heavy memory corruption due to driver + gdrctl interplay. I'm coordinating with infra to isolate those nodes from RDMA path.
Olivia L: SLA check: any customers approaching SLA breach windows?
Lucas H: two customers on dedicated contracts have error budgets under threshold but not yet breached. We need to keep them on fallback.
Maya R: network team applied a micro-config to reduce ECN aggressiveness on ToR. Observed immediate drop in packet retransmits.
Priya S: infra reported firmware patch queued but needs maintenance window if it requires switch reboot. They can hot-patch micro-configs without restart.
Ryan C: after micro-config, container restarts stopped, OOMs almost gone. Still watching for latent corruption.
Maya R: timeline so far: 09:10 alert -> 09:18 initial triage -> 09:25 drain gpu-3a -> 09:32 degraded-mode enabled -> 09:40 network micro-config -> 09:50 visible error rate down to 2%.
Olivia L: good work. Next steps: 1) keep degraded-mode for 1 hour while traffic stabilizes; 2) network to confirm if firmware reboot required; 3) run post-incident validation with synthetic evals and short A/B tests.
Priya S: preparing rollout plan to re-enable normal runtime settings in a canary: flip REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DEGRADED=false on one deployment, run load test for 10m.
Maya R: assigning action owners: Priya - coordinate with infra for firmware window (ticket 2023-IR-889). Ryan - deep logs and follow-up driver/firmware issue. Olivia - customer comms and SLA assessment. Lucas - update all open tickets.
Ryan C: collecting artifacts bundle: /tmp/incident-2136543210.tar.gz (contains dmesg, nvml logs, ib counters, kube events). Uploading to incident storage.
deploy-bot: artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/2136543210/artifacts.tar.gz
Maya R: handoff in 20m to night oncall. Anyone else want to add immediate runbook changes?
Priya S: propose adding RDMA link flapping probe to serving monitors: track port state changes and initiate automatic degraded-mode on >N flaps in M minutes.
Olivia L: endorse. put a PR in infra/monitoring runbooks with alert thresholds.
Lucas H: I'll add a templated customer message for future RDMA fabric incidents.
Maya R: closing notes: incident lowered to monitoring. We'll reconvene if error rate creeps back above 5%.
Olivia L: thanks all, great cross-team coordination. Follow-up postmortem assigned to Ryan and Priya, due EOD tomorrow.
Maya R: leaving final note: timeline and mitigations in the incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2136543210
